basics.name: Joe Pegler
basics.label: Staff-level Blockchain Infrastructure Engineer
basics.specialties: Transaction Systems · EVM + Solana · Protocol Integrations · SDKs
basics.summary: Staff-level blockchain backend and infrastructure engineer designing and operating production transaction systems across EVM and Solana. My work covers execution infrastructure, protocol integrations, multi-chain routing, RPC and simulation paths, and typed SDKs, with particularly deep experience in smart accounts and ERC-4337. I own technical verticals from problem definition and architecture through production rollout, balancing reliability, latency, developer experience, and time-to-market with product and engineering stakeholders. I use AI-assisted workflows for codebase exploration, implementation, testing, debugging, and review while retaining ownership of architecture, correctness, and production decisions.

selectedImpact: Identified execution latency as a production bottleneck at defi.app and replaced third-party transaction infrastructure with an in-house ERC-4337 execution path; powered $100M+ daily trading volume with ~95% swap success and 20–40% faster execution than ZeroDev.

Designed and built @biconomy/abstractjs from scratch as a viem-inspired TypeScript developer product, simplifying wallet, signing, and multi-chain execution through typed APIs, composable abstractions, documentation, and examples; reached ~5.2k weekly npm downloads.

Standardized routing and execution across heterogeneous DEX, bridge, and solver providers (LiFi, Jupiter, 1inch, Odos, Mayan, LayerZero, Relay), placing EVM and Solana simulation and transaction safety behind a consistent typed surface used by frontend and backend teams.

work.summary: Owned production transaction infrastructure across EVM and Solana as a product capability, from route selection and RPC simulation through execution, monitoring, and iteration, translating product journeys into backend systems, APIs, and SDKs.
highlights: Identified execution latency as a production bottleneck and replaced third-party transaction infrastructure with an in-house ERC-4337 bundler, reducing unnecessary simulation and gas-estimation round trips while coordinating wallet pools, nonces, fees, sponsorship, and submission; powered $100M+ daily volume (~5k–7k swaps/day) at ~95% success and 20–40% faster execution than ZeroDev.

Built the reliability and observability layer around pre-submission simulation, guarded retries and fallbacks, ABI/Sourcify-backed error decoding, and structured operational errors, including EntryPoint v7 paths; balanced simulation safety against execution speed while improving production debugging and incident response.

Owned EVM and Solana transaction simulation and sponsorship through production, including Jito-aware Jupiter paths and ATA/CPI safety checks; diagnosed nonce contention, RPC lag, slippage, and simulation-to-execution mismatches, then fed findings back into architecture.

Standardized DEX, bridge, and solver integrations (LiFi, Jupiter, 1inch, Odos, Mayan, LayerZero, Relay) behind RouteClient and ExecutionManager APIs, so frontend and backend teams executed across heterogeneous EVM and Solana protocols through one typed surface.
Automated operational blockchain flows for referral revenue payouts and on-chain claims, and added production outage alerting for execution-path incidents.

work.summary: Owned @biconomy/abstractjs as a developer product for wallet, signing, and multi-chain execution, taking a TypeScript SDK from integration complexity through API design, implementation, documentation, and adoption, with deep ERC-4337 and smart-account coverage.
highlights: Designed and built the SDK from scratch, defining viem-inspired abstraction boundaries, modular clients, typed APIs, composable batching, and account-agnostic execution flows that reduced protocol complexity for application developers.
Took the package through production with documentation and examples for teams integrating gasless and sponsored execution; grew adoption to approximately 5.2k weekly npm downloads.

Implemented wallet and signing infrastructure covering Safe, passkeys/P-256, EIP-712, EIP-1271, ERC-6492, and modular session permissions (ERC-7579), with production safeguards backed by Vitest, Bun, GitHub Actions, and Codecov.

work.summary: Owned application architecture and production delivery for Enso's primary Ethereum dApp, connecting execution UX to protocol routing, GraphQL APIs, and indexing systems.
highlights: Led the application from early product definition through production, shaping execution UX and defining integration boundaries and API contracts with product, protocol, and backend teams.
Built a GraphQL routing API for token-to-token execution paths, alongside Graph Protocol indexing and intent/routing product surfaces, connecting application flows to protocol and blockchain state.
Built the Shortcuts TypeScript SDK covering wallet simulation, balances, and transfer and withdrawal flows, giving application and integration surfaces a typed path into protocol execution.

work.summary: Led engineering delivery for a live trading product, owning interface architecture, team standards, core feature rollout, and release infrastructure.
highlights: Defined interface architecture and engineering standards for the markets and trader UI, guiding feature delivery and team practices on a live exchange product.
Automated CI/CD for the interface stack, improving deployment consistency and reducing release risk in a production trading environment.

earlierExperience: GameAnalytics · Lead Frontend Developer (2016 to 2019): led a team of five, defined architecture and quality standards, and received the company MVP award for 2018/19.
FSI, Healthcare 21, and Nixatel (2013 to 2016): delivered enterprise, mobile, and web products in small engineering teams.
